title: Peanut-Lime Sauce for Soft Noodles
description: Smooth peanut butter and light coconut milk make a pourable Thai-inspired sauce with lime and coconut aminos.

steps.title: Loosen the peanut butter
steps.text: In the cool HexClad, whisk {peanut} with a little {coconut} until smooth. Slowly whisk in the remaining coconut milk.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: Whisk in {broth}, {aminos} and {sugar}. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat and stir for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Add the lime
steps.text: Take the skillet off heat and stir in {lime}.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the finished sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 1/2 cups total. If it measures short, whisk in a little hot water. If it measures over, return it to the skillet and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle over moist chicken or steamed fish while the sauce flows freely from a spoon. For noodles, add extra broth to the sauce, simmer the noodles directly in it and serve them together.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Whisk the peanut butter and coconut milk together a day ahead and chill. Let the mixture warm gradually in the pan. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze in portions for up to 1 month. Add water while reheating to restore a pourable texture. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses lime juice. For gentler Option B, omit the lime and use a little more broth. Both versions are dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 69 kcal, 2.1 g protein, 3.9 g total carbohydrate, 5.4 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 42 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
